### R0 definition (what is switched off)

R0 = the baseline G2: raw model output, minimal merge. doc_type of the first parsed page; every header field is the first non-null value over the pages in page order ("any page"); rows concatenated in page order with repeated column-header rows and all-null rows KEPT; no normalisation (values only stripped / str()-ed, which the scorer ignores); no OCR. Not a rule, on in every rung: only the 4 row keys are kept, a waybill has no line_items, a page that failed to parse is None (0 failed pages in this run). Rungs add one rule each, cumulatively, in the order below; R3/R4 are confidence-only and are not rungs.

### (d) Confidence-only rules R3 / R4 (dev100 predictions of the R8 rung)

Flags cannot change a value (`validate_doc` returns flags only; this script asserts the prediction is byte-identical before and after, `tests/test_validate.py` asserts it on synthetic docs). Criterion for KEEP as a confidence feature: on real dev errors, n_wrong >= 5, recall of errors >= 50% and flag precision >= 2x the base error rate; with fewer than 5 real errors the flag is NOT ASSESSABLE on real data and the decision rests on the SYNTHETIC injection table plus the gold false-alarm count.

### R1 detail: does per-cluster inference add anything over per-document resolution?

Layout clusters (OCR keyword+position signature of page 1, KMeans seed 42, k=28 chosen by silhouette 0.502 over k=8..30, fit on 400 train+dev invoice pages, no labels, no test). Diagnostic only: ARI vs supplier group 0.346, purity 0.645. On the dev100 run the model emitted dates as ISO in 72/72 cases, so R1a/R1b receive no ambiguous input and change 0 / 0 values.

SYNTHETIC raw variants (all 384 train+dev gold dates re-printed; counts of correct / left raw & flagged / wrong ISO):

| scenario | mode | correct | unresolved | wrong | pools with an inferred order |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| seen_formats | raw_untouched | 44 | 340 | 0 | 7/18 |
| seen_formats | per_document | 384 | 0 | 0 | - |
| seen_formats | predicted_cluster | 384 | 0 | 0 | 13/28 |
| seen_formats | oracle_group | 384 | 0 | 0 | 7/18 |
| numeric_stress | raw_untouched | 0 | 384 | 0 | 18/18 |
| numeric_stress | per_document | 303 | 81 | 0 | - |
| numeric_stress | predicted_cluster | 335 | 46 | 3 | 17/28 |
| numeric_stress | oracle_group | 384 | 0 | 0 | 18/18 |

Reading: on the five seen formats per-document resolution already resolves every date, so the cluster step adds nothing there (recon section 4: numeric-format groups have 0 gold dates with day <= 12). It only matters for an unseen numeric format with day <= 12 dates (numeric_stress). With label-free clusters of low purity it recovers part of them and can mis-pool suppliers that print opposite orders (the `wrong` column): every such date carries the flag `date_order_inferred` and must take the Phase 5 confidence penalty. Dates left raw keep the flag `date_ambiguous`.

Fail-closed check on the dev100 outputs: of 12 cells changed by the value-changing rules (R0 -> R8), 0 are not a re-formatting of the raw value (digits changed, or the new value not contained in the raw one). R3/R4 return flags only (asserted: predictions byte-identical before/after validation).

R3 / R4 (confidence features): KEPT as inputs to the later confidence model; their informativeness on REAL errors is NOT ASSESSABLE on dev100 (wrong non-null values per flag: currency 0, airports 0, AWB 0, HAWB 2; the criterion needs >= 5). Support: no false alarms on the gold values of train+dev (table above) and 100% catch of injected format-breaking errors. Limitation: same-class digit/letter substitutions are not caught by the shape checks (AWB/HAWB) and only partly by IATA membership, so these flags detect structural misreads, not wrong-but-well-formed values.

Overall G3 (full pipeline R8 vs R0): d OVERALL = +0.49 [+0.00, +1.28], false-fill 0.00 -> 0.00; CI excludes 0: NO. The strict spec gate is therefore NOT met by Phase 3 as a whole on dev100. The pipeline is retained because the only measured movement is a gain with no loss and the remaining rules are no-ops on this model's output (safety nets), not because a benefit was demonstrated; Step U (500 docs) re-gates.

## Sources and licenses of the bundled code lists (G3 R3)

- `meta/iata_airports.txt`: OurAirports `airports.csv`, column `iata_code`, fetched 2026-10-02, 9051 codes. License: public domain, per https://ourairports.com/data/ (stated by the publisher; read from the source site by the executor, not independently re-checked).
- ISO 4217 currency codes: no longer vendored. `shipdoc.validate.iso4217_codes()` reads `pycountry.currencies` (`alpha_3`) from the locked runtime dependency `pycountry` 26.2.16. Licence: LGPL-2.1 (`License-Expression: LGPL-2.1-only` and the LGPLv2 classifier in `pycountry-26.2.16.dist-info/METADATA`; terms in `pycountry-26.2.16.dist-info/licenses/LICENSE.txt` and `pycountry/COPYRIGHT.txt`, both read from the installed package). The ISO 4217 data inside pycountry (`pycountry/databases/iso4217.json`) is a copy of Debian's pkg-isocodes (iso-codes) database, as stated in the same METADATA; the licence of that data itself was not read here and is UNVERIFIED. pycountry's list has 178 codes, identical (set equality, checked once with the removed SIX-derived file `meta/iso4217.txt`, SIX `list-one.xml` published 2026-09-17) to the file it replaces, so the G3 ladder is unaffected.
- Both lists are membership tests used as confidence features only; they never change an extracted value (spec section 2).
